source.text: Οὐκ ἔστιν μαθητὴς ὑπὲρ τὸν διδάσκαλον οὐδὲ δοῦλος ὑπὲρ τὸν κύριον αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Not is a disciple above the teacher nor a slave above the master of him.

en.L: A disciple is not above the teacher, nor a slave above {{gender:their|his}} master.
en.B: No disciple ranks above the teacher, and no servant above the master.
en.R: Students are not more important than their teacher. Servants are not more important than their master.

es.L: No hay discípulo por encima del maestro, ni esclavo por encima de su señor.
es.B: Ningún discípulo es superior a su maestro, ni ningún siervo a su señor.
es.R: Un alumno no es más importante que su maestro. Un siervo no es más importante que su señor.

fr.L: Un disciple n’est pas au-dessus du maître, ni un esclave au-dessus de son seigneur.
fr.B: Aucun disciple n’est au-dessus de son maître, et aucun serviteur au-dessus de son seigneur.
fr.R: Un élève n’est pas plus important que celui qui l’enseigne. Un serviteur n’est pas plus important que son maître.

sw.L: Mwanafunzi hayuko juu ya mwalimu, wala mtumwa juu ya bwana wake.
sw.B: Hakuna mwanafunzi aliye juu ya mwalimu wake, wala mtumishi aliye juu ya bwana wake.
sw.R: Mwanafunzi si muhimu kuliko mwalimu wake. Mtumishi si muhimu kuliko bwana wake.

vi.L: Môn đồ không hơn thầy, nô lệ cũng không hơn chủ mình.
vi.B: Không có môn đồ nào hơn thầy, cũng không có đầy tớ nào hơn chủ.
vi.R: Học trò không quan trọng hơn thầy mình. Đầy tớ cũng không quan trọng hơn chủ mình.

ko.L: 제자가 스승보다 높지 않고, 종이 자기 주인보다 높지 않다.
ko.B: 제자가 스승보다 높을 수 없고, 종이 주인보다 높을 수 없다.
ko.R: 제자는 스승보다 더 높은 사람이 아니다. 종도 주인보다 더 높은 사람이 아니다.

pt.L: Não há discípulo acima do mestre, nem escravo acima do seu senhor.
pt.B: Nenhum discípulo está acima do mestre, e nenhum servo está acima do seu senhor.
pt.R: Os alunos não são mais importantes que o professor. Os servos não são mais importantes que o seu senhor.

decisions.choice: not above the teacher: followers will be treated as their master is
alternatives: a rule about respect for teachers
decisions.reason: The proverb explains why the disciples will be persecuted: Jesus has been, so they will be (10:25).

decisions.choice: slave: one owned by a master and bound to serve him
decisions.reason: The word is the one for a slave. Jesus and Paul use it of those who belong wholly to God (Philippians 1:1).

decisions.choice: {{gender:their|his}}
decisions.reason: The proverb applies to all disciples, so the inclusive form is the default.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m2) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: le maître (teacher) and son seigneur (master) (L, B); celui qui l’enseigne and son maître (R)
decisions.reason: French "maître" can mean both teacher and master, so the two words of the proverb need different French words. Literal and Balanced keep "maître" for the teacher, as in Luke 6:40, and use "seigneur" for the slave's owner; Readable, which speaks of a pupil, says "celui qui l’enseigne" and keeps "maître" for the servant's master. The same in 10:25.

decisions.choice: "son seigneur" with no gender span (L)
alternatives: a gender span on the possessive
decisions.reason: The English Literal needs {{gender:their|his}}; the French possessive agrees with the thing possessed and does not show the owner's sex, so no setting is needed. The same holds for "son maître", "sa croix", "sa vie" and "sa récompense" in 10:25-42.

decisions.choice: mtumwa (L); mtumishi (B, R); bwana, lowercase
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice: Literal says what the man was, one owned by a master (meaning decision m2); Balanced and Readable say "mtumishi", as the English says "servant". The master is the owner in the saying, so "bwana" is lowercase, as in John 13:16.

decisions.choice: esclavo (L); siervo (B, R); señor
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for this word: Literal says what the man was, one owned by a master (meaning decision m2); Balanced and Readable say "siervo", as the English says "servant". "Señor" for the master, as in John 13:16.

decisions.choice: "nô lệ" (L); "đầy tớ" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The style guide's rule for doulos, as the English. "mình" already covers men and women, so the English Literal gender span has no counterpart; the same in 10:25.

decisions.choice: "học trò" (R) for "disciple"
decisions.reason: The saying is a general proverb about any pupil and teacher, as the English Readable "students" shows; Literal and Balanced keep "môn đồ", the word for Jesus's disciples, so the link to them stays visible.

decisions.choice: "제자", "스승", "종", "주인" at every level; no gender span
decisions.reason: "제자" is the word for disciples at every level (docs/korean-style.md section 6), so Readable keeps it where the English Readable says "students". "종" is the style guide's word for doulos at every level and already covers both the English "slave" and "servant"; slavery itself is not the point here. Korean needs no pronoun for the master's servant, so the English gender span has nothing to change.

decisions.choice: escravo (L); servo (B, R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 6), as the English: Literal says what the word means, one who is owned; Balanced and Readable say "servo", and the meaning note (m2) keeps the sense of ownership.

decisions.choice: do seu senhor, with no gender setting
alternatives: a gender setting on the possessive
decisions.reason: Here and throughout this passage (10:25, 38, 39, 42) the English needs a setting to choose between "their" and "his". Portuguese "seu, sua" agrees with the thing owned, not with the owner, so it is already inclusive and takes no setting.

source.text: ἀρκετὸν τῷ μαθητῇ ἵνα γένηται ὡς ὁ διδάσκαλος αὐτοῦ, καὶ ὁ δοῦλος ὡς ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Enough for the disciple that he become as the teacher of him, and the slave as the master of him.

en.L: [It is] enough for the disciple to become like {{gender:their|his}} teacher, and the slave like {{gender:their|his}} master.
en.B: It is enough for disciples to become like their teacher, and for servants to become like their master.
en.R: Students should be content to become like their teacher. Servants should be content to become like their master.

es.L: [Es] suficiente para el discípulo llegar a ser como su maestro, y para el esclavo, como su señor.
es.B: Para un discípulo es suficiente llegar a ser como su maestro, y para un siervo, llegar a ser como su señor.
es.R: El alumno debe estar contento si llega a ser como su maestro. El siervo debe estar contento si llega a ser como su señor.

fr.L: Il suffit au disciple de devenir comme son maître, et à l’esclave comme son seigneur.
fr.B: Il suffit aux disciples de devenir comme leur maître, et aux serviteurs comme leur seigneur.
fr.R: L’élève doit être content de devenir comme celui qui l’enseigne. Le serviteur doit être content de devenir comme son maître.

sw.L: Inatosha kwa mwanafunzi kwamba afanane na mwalimu wake, na mtumwa [afanane] na bwana wake.
sw.B: Inamtosha mwanafunzi kufanana na mwalimu wake, na mtumishi kufanana na bwana wake.
sw.R: Mwanafunzi aridhike akiwa kama mwalimu wake. Mtumishi aridhike akiwa kama bwana wake.

vi.L: Môn đồ được như thầy mình, và nô lệ được như chủ mình, [thế là] đủ rồi.
vi.B: Môn đồ được như thầy, đầy tớ được như chủ, thế là đủ rồi.
vi.R: Học trò nên bằng lòng khi được giống như thầy mình. Đầy tớ nên bằng lòng khi được giống như chủ mình.

ko.L: 제자가 자기 스승처럼 되고, 종이 자기 주인처럼 되면 [그것으로] 충분하다.
ko.B: 제자는 스승처럼 되고, 종은 주인처럼 되면 그것으로 충분하다.
ko.R: 제자는 스승과 같은 대접을 받는 것으로 만족해야 한다. 종도 주인과 같은 대접을 받는 것으로 만족해야 한다.

pt.L: [É] suficiente ao discípulo que se torne como o seu mestre, e o escravo, como o seu senhor.
pt.B: Já é bastante para o discípulo chegar a ser como o mestre, e para o servo, como o senhor.
pt.R: Os alunos devem se contentar em ficar iguais ao professor. Os servos devem se contentar em ficar iguais ao seu senhor.

decisions.choice: enough: they should expect no better treatment than their master's
decisions.reason: To share the master's lot is both all they can expect and an honor.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: "같은 대접을 받는 것으로 만족해야 한다" (R)
decisions.reason: Enough means they should expect no better treatment than their master's (meaning decision); Readable says so, as the English Readable says "be content".

source.text: εἰ τὸν οἰκοδεσπότην Βεελζεβοὺλ ἐπεκάλεσαν, πόσῳ μᾶλλον τοὺς οἰκιακοὺς αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: If the master of the house Beelzebul they called, how much more the household of him.

en.L: If they called the master of the house Beelzebul, how much more those of his household!
en.B: If they have called the head of the house Beelzebul, how much more will they insult the members of his household!
en.R: People have called the head of the house Beelzebul, the ruler of demons. So they will be even quicker to insult the rest of his family.

es.L: Si al dueño de la casa llamaron Beelzebul, ¡cuánto más a los de su casa!
es.B: Si al jefe de la casa lo han llamado Beelzebul, ¡cuánto más insultarán a los de su familia!
es.R: La gente ha llamado Beelzebul, el jefe de los demonios, al jefe de la casa. Por eso insultarán todavía más al resto de su familia.

fr.L: S’ils ont appelé le maître de la maison Béelzéboul, combien plus ceux de sa maison !
fr.B: Si l’on a traité le chef de famille de Béelzéboul, à combien plus forte raison insultera-t-on les gens de sa maison !
fr.R: Des gens ont appelé le chef de la maison Béelzéboul, le chef des démons. Alors ils insulteront encore plus facilement le reste de sa famille.

sw.L: Ikiwa mwenye nyumba walimwita Beelzebuli, sembuse watu wa nyumba yake!
sw.B: Ikiwa mkuu wa nyumba wamemwita Beelzebuli, watawatukana zaidi sana watu wa nyumba yake!
sw.R: Watu wamemwita mkuu wa nyumba Beelzebuli, yaani mkuu wa pepo. Kwa hiyo watawatukana hata zaidi watu wengine wa familia yake.

vi.L: Nếu người ta đã gọi chủ nhà là Bê-ên-xê-bun, thì những người nhà của ông càng [bị gọi như vậy] biết bao!
vi.B: Nếu người ta đã gọi chủ nhà là Bê-ên-xê-bun, thì họ còn sỉ nhục những người trong nhà ông đến đâu nữa!
vi.R: Người ta đã gọi chủ nhà là Bê-ên-xê-bun, tức là kẻ cầm đầu các quỷ. Vậy họ lại càng dễ sỉ nhục những người khác trong gia đình ông hơn nữa.

ko.L: 그들이 집주인을 바알세불이라고 불렀다면, 그의 집 식구들은 얼마나 더 [그렇게 부르겠느냐]!
ko.B: 사람들이 집주인을 바알세불이라고 불렀다면, 그 집 식구들은 얼마나 더 심한 모욕을 당하겠느냐!
ko.R: 사람들은 집주인을 귀신들의 우두머리인 바알세불이라고 불렀다. 그러니 그 집의 다른 식구들은 더욱더 심한 욕을 듣게 될 것이다.

pt.L: Se ao dono da casa chamaram de Belzebu, quanto mais aos da sua casa!
pt.B: Se chamaram de Belzebu o chefe da casa, quanto mais vão insultar os membros da família dele!
pt.R: As pessoas chamaram o chefe da casa de Belzebu, o chefe dos demônios. Então vão insultar mais depressa ainda o resto da família dele.

decisions.choice: Beelzebul: a name for Satan, the ruler of the demons
decisions.reason: The name recalls Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron (2 Kings 1:2). In the Gospels it is a name for the prince of demons (12:24-27). It echoes the charge of 9:34.

decisions.choice: Beelzebul, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: Beelzebub, the reading of some Latin and Syriac witnesses
Beezebul, the spelling of a few Greek manuscripts
decisions.reason: The spelling "Beelzebub" follows 2 Kings 1:2 and is familiar from older translations, but the Greek manuscripts read "Beelzebul" or "Beezebul". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the master of the house: Jesus himself
decisions.reason: Jesus is the one called Beelzebul (9:34; 12:24). Some suggest a play on words, as "zebul" may mean "dwelling", making Beelzebul "lord of the house".

decisions.choice: his household, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The master of the house is a figure in a picture, so the pronoun takes no span, though the picture points to Jesus.

decisions.choice: the ruler of demons
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the name and says who is meant.

decisions.choice: Beelzebuli
decisions.reason: The name in the spelling of the text translated (meaning decision m2), with the final vowel Swahili adds to names (Danieli, Samweli).

decisions.choice: Beelzebul
decisions.reason: The spelling of the text translated (meaning decision m2). "Belcebú" is the familiar Spanish form, from the spelling "Beelzebub" in other manuscripts and the Latin.

decisions.choice: "Bê-ên-xê-bun"; "ông" for the master of the house, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The Protestant spelling, as in Mark 3:22. The master of the house is Jesus (meaning decision), but he speaks of him through the picture, so the pronoun belongs to the picture, as the English decision says.

decisions.choice: "바알세불"; "집주인" without honorific
decisions.reason: "바알세불" is the Protestant form used in the Korean Mark 3:22, a name for Satan (meaning decision). The master of the house is Jesus himself (meaning decision), but he speaks of himself in a picture, and a Korean speaker does not use honorifics of himself, so "집주인" stays plain, as the English has no deity_pronoun span here.

decisions.choice: Belzebu
decisions.reason: For the whole book (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 11): "Belzebu" is the form Portuguese readers know. It hides the difference between the manuscripts' "-bul" and the older "-bub" that the meaning note (m2) discusses, which the note keeps.

source.text: Μὴ οὖν φοβηθῆτε αὐτούς· οὐδὲν γάρ ἐστιν κεκαλυμμένον ὃ οὐκ ἀποκαλυφθήσεται, καὶ κρυπτὸν ὃ οὐ γνωσθήσεται.

records.literal_gloss: Not therefore you should fear them; nothing for is covered which not will be revealed, and hidden which not will be known.

en.L: So do not fear them; for nothing is covered that will not be revealed, and [nothing] hidden that will not be known.
en.B: So do not be afraid of them. Everything now covered will be uncovered, and every secret will come to light.
en.R: So do not be afraid of those people. Everything that is hidden now will be shown. Every secret will be made known.

es.L: Por tanto, no {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo de ellos; pues no hay nada cubierto que no vaya a ser revelado, ni escondido que no vaya a ser conocido.
es.B: Así que no les {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo. Todo lo que ahora está cubierto será descubierto, y todo secreto saldrá a la luz.
es.R: Así que no les {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo a esas personas. Todo lo que ahora está escondido se va a mostrar. Todo secreto se va a conocer.

fr.L: Ne les craignez donc pas ; car rien n’est couvert qui ne sera découvert, ni caché qui ne sera connu.
fr.B: N’ayez donc pas peur d’eux. Tout ce qui est maintenant couvert sera découvert, et tout secret viendra au grand jour.
fr.R: N’ayez donc pas peur de ces gens. Tout ce qui est caché maintenant sera montré. Chaque secret sera connu.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo msiwaogope; maana hakuna kitu kilichofunikwa ambacho hakitafunuliwa, wala kilichofichwa ambacho hakitajulikana.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo msiwaogope. Kila kilichofunikwa sasa kitafunuliwa, na kila siri itajulikana wazi.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo msiwaogope watu hao. Kila kitu kilichofichwa sasa kitaonyeshwa. Kila siri itajulikana.

vi.L: Vậy đừng sợ họ; vì không có gì che giấu mà sẽ không bị bày tỏ ra, và [không có gì] bí mật mà sẽ không được biết đến.
vi.B: Vậy, đừng sợ họ. Mọi điều đang bị che đậy sẽ được bày tỏ ra, và mọi điều bí mật sẽ được mọi người biết.
vi.R: Vậy đừng sợ những người ấy. Mọi điều bây giờ đang bị giấu kín rồi sẽ được bày ra. Mọi điều bí mật rồi sẽ được mọi người biết.

ko.L: 그러므로 그들을 두려워하지 마라. 덮여 있는 것 가운데 드러나지 않을 것이 없고, 숨겨진 것 가운데 알려지지 않을 것이 없기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그러므로 그들을 두려워하지 마라. 지금 덮여 있는 것은 모두 드러나고, 숨겨진 것은 모두 알려질 것이다.
ko.R: 그러니 그런 사람들을 무서워하지 마라. 지금 숨겨져 있는 것은 모두 드러날 것이다. 비밀은 모두 알려지게 될 것이다.

pt.L: Portanto, não os temam; pois não há nada encoberto que não venha a ser revelado, nem [nada] oculto que não venha a ser conhecido.
pt.B: Por isso, não tenham medo deles. Tudo o que agora está coberto será descoberto, e todo segredo virá à luz.
pt.R: Por isso, não tenham medo dessas pessoas. Tudo o que agora está escondido vai ser mostrado. Todo segredo vai ser conhecido.

decisions.choice: what is covered will be revealed: the message now spoken in private will be made public
decisions.reason: Verse 27 applies the saying to Jesus's teaching. Whatever their enemies do, the truth will come out. The same saying is used of exposing sin in Luke 12:2-3.

decisions.choice: do not fear them: the persecutors of 10:17-25
decisions.reason: "Them" refers to those who will hate and persecute the disciples. "Do not fear" comes three times (10:26, 28, 31).

decisions.choice: plural_you spans on the verbs and pronouns addressed to the Twelve: tengan|tengáis
decisions.reason: Spanish has two plural forms of "you", Latin American "ustedes" and Peninsular "vosotros"; the setting chooses between them. English has no such choice, so these spans have no English counterpart. The same throughout the passage.

source.text: ὃ λέγω ὑμῖν ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ, εἴπατε ἐν τῷ φωτί· καὶ ὃ εἰς τὸ οὖς ἀκούετε, κηρύξατε ἐπὶ τῶν δωμάτων.

records.literal_gloss: What I say to you in the darkness, say in the light; and what into the ear you hear, proclaim on the housetops.

en.L: What I tell you in the darkness, speak in the light; and what you hear in the ear, proclaim on the housetops.
en.B: The things I tell you in the dark, you must say in the open; the things you hear as a whisper, you must proclaim from the housetops.
en.R: I am telling you things now in private. Tell them openly to everyone. What you hear from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in a whisper, shout from the rooftops.

es.L: Lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} digo en la oscuridad, {{plural_you:díganlo|decidlo}} a la luz; y lo que {{plural_you:escuchan|escucháis}} al oído, {{plural_you:anúncienlo|anunciadlo}} sobre las azoteas.
es.B: Lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} digo a oscuras, {{plural_you:repítanlo|repetidlo}} a la luz del día; lo que {{plural_you:oyen|oís}} en un susurro, {{plural_you:proclámenlo|proclamadlo}} desde las azoteas.
es.R: Ahora {{plural_you:les|os}} digo cosas en privado. {{plural_you:Cuéntenlas|Contadlas}} abiertamente a todos. Lo que {{plural_you:oyen|oís}} de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} en voz baja, {{plural_you:grítenlo|gritadlo}} desde los techos de las casas.

fr.L: Ce que je vous dis dans les ténèbres, dites-le dans la lumière ; et ce que vous entendez à l’oreille, proclamez-le sur les toits.
fr.B: Ce que je vous dis dans l’obscurité, dites-le en plein jour ; ce qu’on vous murmure à l’oreille, proclamez-le du haut des toits.
fr.R: En ce moment, je vous dis des choses en privé. Dites-les ouvertement à tout le monde. Ce que vous {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}entendez dire tout bas, criez-le du haut des toits.

sw.L: Ninayowaambia katika giza, yasemeni katika nuru; na mnayoyasikia sikioni, yatangazeni juu ya mapaa.
sw.B: Mambo ninayowaambia gizani, myaseme mahali pa wazi; mnayoyasikia kwa kunong'onezwa, myatangaze kutoka juu ya mapaa ya nyumba.
sw.R: Sasa ninawaambia mambo kwa faragha. Yaelezeni waziwazi kwa kila mtu. Mnayoyasikia kutoka {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}} kwa sauti ya chini, yatangazeni kwa sauti kubwa kutoka juu ya mapaa.

vi.L: Điều {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con trong bóng tối, hãy nói ra giữa ánh sáng; và điều các con nghe [nói] vào tai, hãy rao giảng trên mái nhà.
vi.B: Những điều {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con trong bóng tối, các con hãy nói ra giữa ánh sáng. Những điều các con nghe nói nhỏ bên tai, hãy rao lớn từ trên mái nhà.
vi.R: Bây giờ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đang nói riêng với các con. Hãy nói những điều ấy công khai cho mọi người. Những gì các con nghe {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói thầm bên tai, hãy nói lớn lên từ trên mái nhà.

ko.L: 내가 너희에게 어둠 속에서 말하는 것을 너희는 빛 가운데서 말하고, 너희가 귀에 대고 [하는 말로] 듣는 것을 지붕 위에서 선포하여라.
ko.B: 내가 너희에게 어두운 데서 말하는 것을 너희는 밝은 데서 말하여라. 귓속말로 듣는 것을 너희는 지붕 위에서 외쳐라.
ko.R: 내가 지금 너희에게만 조용히 말하는 것을 너희는 모든 사람에게 드러내 놓고 말하여라. 나에게서 귓속말로 들은 것을 지붕 위에 올라가 큰 소리로 외쳐라.

pt.L: O que eu lhes digo na escuridão, digam na luz; e o que ouvem no ouvido, proclamem sobre os telhados.
pt.B: O que eu lhes digo no escuro, vocês devem dizer às claras; o que ouvem em sussurro, devem proclamar do alto dos telhados.
pt.R: Agora eu estou contando coisas a vocês em particular. Contem essas coisas abertamente a todos. O que vocês ouvem de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} em voz baixa, gritem de cima dos telhados.

decisions.choice: in the dark, in the light: in private, in public
decisions.reason: Darkness and light stand for what is hidden and what is open. Jesus teaches the twelve privately; they must tell it to all.

decisions.choice: the housetops: flat roofs, a place to call out to the whole street
decisions.reason: Houses had flat roofs reached by stairs, and announcements could be made from them.

decisions.choice: as a whisper
decisions.reason: "In the ear" means spoken quietly to one person.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}
decisions.reason: The English "me" takes the setting; Swahili carries most pronouns for Jesus inside the verb (ninawaambia), where there is nothing to capitalise, so only free pronouns and possessives take the span, as in John. The same throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: las azoteas (L, B); los techos de las casas (R)
decisions.reason: The roofs were flat, a place to stand and call to the whole street (meaning decision m2). "Azotea" is a flat roof one can walk on; "tejado" is a sloping tiled roof.

decisions.choice: "trên mái nhà"
decisions.reason: The flat roofs were a place to call out to the whole street (meaning decision); "mái nhà" keeps the Bible's picture, and the verb "rao" (announce aloud) shows its use.

decisions.choice: "너희에게만 조용히" and "모든 사람에게 드러내 놓고" (R)
decisions.reason: Dark and light mean private and public (meaning decision); Readable says what the picture means, as the English Readable does. Flat roofs were a place to call out to the whole street (meaning decision), so "지붕 위" stays at every level.

decisions.choice: os telhados
decisions.reason: The roofs were flat (m2), which "terraço" would say, but "terraço" suggests a balcony or a modern rooftop terrace. "Telhados" is the plain word for the top of a house, and "do alto dos telhados" keeps the picture of calling out over the street.

source.text: καὶ μὴ φοβεῖσθε ἀπὸ τῶν ἀποκτεννόντων τὸ σῶμα τὴν δὲ ψυχὴν μὴ δυναμένων ἀποκτεῖναι· φοβεῖσθε δὲ μᾶλλον τὸν δυνάμενον καὶ ψυχὴν καὶ σῶμα ἀπολέσαι ἐν γεέννῃ.

records.literal_gloss: And not be afraid of the killing the body, the but soul not being able to kill; fear but rather the being able both soul and body to destroy in Gehenna.

en.L: And do not be afraid of those who kill the body but are not able to kill the soul; but rather fear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} who is able to destroy both soul and body in Gehenna.
en.B: Those who kill the body have no power to kill the soul, so do not be afraid of them. Be afraid instead of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} who can destroy soul and body alike in hell.
en.R: Do not be afraid of people. They can kill your body, but they cannot kill your soul. The one you should fear is God. He can destroy both your body and your soul in hell.

es.L: Y no {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo de los que matan el cuerpo, pero no pueden matar el alma; más bien {{plural_you:tengan|tened}} miedo del que puede destruir tanto el alma como el cuerpo en [la] Gehena.
es.B: Los que matan el cuerpo no tienen poder para matar el alma; así que no les {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo. {{plural_you:Teman|Temed}} más bien al que puede destruir alma y cuerpo a la vez en el infierno.
es.R: No {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo de la gente. Pueden matar el cuerpo, pero no pueden matar el alma. Al que {{plural_you:deben|debéis}} temer es a Dios. Él puede destruir en el infierno tanto el cuerpo como el alma.

fr.L: Et ne craignez pas ceux qui tuent le corps mais ne peuvent pas tuer l’âme ; craignez plutôt celui qui peut faire périr à la fois l’âme et le corps dans la géhenne.
fr.B: Ceux qui tuent le corps n’ont pas le pouvoir de tuer l’âme ; n’ayez donc pas peur d’eux. Craignez plutôt celui qui peut faire périr l’âme aussi bien que le corps en enfer.
fr.R: N’ayez pas peur des gens. Ils peuvent tuer votre corps, mais ils ne peuvent pas tuer votre âme. Celui dont vous devez avoir peur, c’est Dieu. Il peut détruire à la fois votre corps et votre âme en enfer.

sw.L: Na msiwaogope wale wanaoua mwili lakini hawawezi kuiua nafsi; bali mwogopeni zaidi {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} anayeweza kuangamiza nafsi na mwili pia katika Gehena.
sw.B: Wale wanaoua mwili hawana uwezo wa kuua nafsi, kwa hiyo msiwaogope. Badala yake mwogopeni {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} anayeweza kuangamiza nafsi na mwili pamoja katika jehanamu.
sw.R: Msiwaogope watu. Wanaweza kuua mwili wenu, lakini hawawezi kuua nafsi zenu. Mnayepaswa kumwogopa ni Mungu. Yeye anaweza kuangamiza mwili wenu na nafsi zenu katika jehanamu.

vi.L: Và đừng sợ những kẻ giết thân thể nhưng không thể giết linh hồn; nhưng thà hãy sợ Đấng có thể hủy diệt cả linh hồn lẫn thân thể trong Ghê-hen-na.
vi.B: Những kẻ giết thân thể không thể giết được linh hồn, vậy đừng sợ họ. Nhưng hãy sợ Đấng có thể hủy diệt cả linh hồn lẫn thân thể trong địa ngục.
vi.R: Đừng sợ người ta. Họ có thể giết thân thể các con, nhưng không thể giết linh hồn các con. Đấng các con phải kính sợ là Đức Chúa Trời. Ngài có thể hủy diệt cả thân thể lẫn linh hồn các con trong địa ngục.

ko.L: 그리고 몸은 죽여도 영혼은 죽일 수 없는 자들을 두려워하지 마라. 오히려 영혼과 몸을 둘 다 게헨나에서 멸망시키실 수 있는 분을 두려워하여라.
ko.B: 몸은 죽여도 영혼은 죽이지 못하는 사람들을 두려워하지 마라. 오히려 영혼과 몸을 함께 지옥에서 멸망시키실 수 있는 분을 두려워하여라.
ko.R: 사람들을 무서워하지 마라. 그들은 너희 몸을 죽일 수는 있어도 너희 영혼은 죽이지 못한다. 너희가 두려워해야 할 분은 하나님이시다. 하나님께서는 너희 몸과 영혼을 둘 다 지옥에서 멸망시키실 수 있다.

pt.L: E não temam os que matam o corpo, mas não podem matar a alma; temam, antes, {{deity_pronoun:aquele|Aquele}} que pode destruir tanto a alma como o corpo na geena.
pt.B: Os que matam o corpo não têm poder para matar a alma; por isso, não tenham medo deles. Tenham medo, isso sim, {{deity_pronoun:daquele|Daquele}} que pode destruir no inferno tanto a alma como o corpo.
pt.R: Não tenham medo das pessoas. Elas podem matar o corpo de vocês, mas não podem matar a alma de vocês. Quem vocês devem temer é Deus. Ele pode destruir no inferno tanto o corpo como a alma de vocês.

decisions.choice: the one who is able to destroy: God
decisions.reason: Only God judges and destroys in Gehenna (Isaiah 66:24; James 4:12). The next verses speak of the same God as a caring Father, so fear of him goes with trust.

decisions.choice: soul: the person's life and self beyond bodily death
decisions.reason: Here the word means the part of a person that killing the body cannot reach.

decisions.choice: Gehenna: the place of final judgment
decisions.reason: As in 5:22, Gehenna was the valley of Hinnom by Jerusalem, whose name became a name for the fire of God's judgment.

decisions.choice: destroy: ruin in the final judgment
decisions.reason: The word means to ruin or destroy. Whether this means ending existence or lasting ruin is not settled by this verse (compare 25:46).

decisions.choice: Gehenna (L); hell (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:22, Literal keeps the place name.

decisions.choice: The one you should fear is God.
decisions.reason: Readable names God, following the meaning decision.

decisions.choice: la géhenne (L); l’enfer (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the style guide (section 9): French follows the English per level, keeping the place name at Literal and saying "hell" at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: "celui qui" for God with no deity_pronoun span (L, B)
decisions.reason: The English puts the setting on "him"; French says "celui qui", a demonstrative, which the French setting does not cover, as in Luke 12:5 and 10:16. The same for "celui qui m’a envoyé" in 10:40.

decisions.choice: Gehena (L); jehanamu (B, R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice: Literal keeps the name of the place, Balanced and Readable say "jehanamu", the Swahili word for the place of final judgment (meaning decision m3), as the English says "hell".

decisions.choice: nafsi
decisions.reason: The soul as the person's life and self beyond bodily death (meaning decision m2). "Roho" is also the word for spirit and for the Holy Spirit; "nafsi" is the self.

decisions.choice: Gehena (L); el infierno (B, R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice: Literal keeps the name of the place, Balanced and Readable say what it stands for, the place of final judgment (meaning decision m3), as the English says "hell".

decisions.choice: del que (L), al que (B), with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: English "him" for God takes the setting. Spanish says "the one who" with the article, "el que", which is not a pronoun, so there is nothing to capitalise. Where Spanish has a separate pronoun for God or for Jesus (mí, me, mi, lo, él, su), it takes the span, as in verse 27.

decisions.choice: "Ghê-hen-na" (L); "địa ngục" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 9:43-47: Literal keeps the place name, the other levels the common Protestant word for the place of final judgment (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "Đấng" (L, B) for "the one who is able"
decisions.reason: The one who can destroy is God (meaning decision). Vietnamese has no pronoun in this place; "Đấng", the noun for a revered being, shows who is meant and is always capitalised, so it takes no setting span. Readable names God, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "영혼" for psyche here
decisions.reason: The style guide's word for psyche is "목숨", but here the word is set against the body and means the self that lives on beyond bodily death (meaning decision); "목숨" would say the soul can be killed by no one, which loses the contrast. 10:39 keeps "목숨".

decisions.choice: "게헨나" (L); "지옥" (B, R); "멸망시키실 수 있는 분" with honorific
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Mark 9:43-47. The one able to destroy is God (meaning decision), so Jesus speaks of him with the honorific -시- and "분"; Readable names him, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: a geena (L); o inferno (B, R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 6), as the English: Literal keeps the place name, lowercased like a common noun as Portuguese writes it; Balanced and Readable say "inferno".

source.text: οὐχὶ δύο στρουθία ἀσσαρίου πωλεῖται;

records.literal_gloss: Not two sparrows for an assarion are sold?

en.L: Are not two sparrows sold for an assarion?
en.B: Two sparrows sell for {{units:a penny|an assarion}}, do they not?
en.R: Two sparrows are sold for only {{units:a penny|an assarion}}.

es.L: ¿No se venden dos gorriones por un as?
es.B: ¿No se venden dos gorriones por {{units:menos de una hora de salario|un as}}?
es.R: Dos gorriones se venden por solo {{units:lo que se gana en menos de una hora|un as}}.

fr.L: Deux moineaux ne se vendent-ils pas un as ?
fr.B: On vend deux moineaux pour {{units:un centime|un as}}, n’est-ce pas ?
fr.R: Deux moineaux se vendent pour {{units:un centime|un as}} seulement.

sw.L: Je, shomoro wawili hawauzwi kwa asarioni moja?
sw.B: Je, shomoro wawili hawauzwi kwa {{units:mshahara wa chini ya saa moja|asarioni moja}}?
sw.R: Shomoro wawili huuzwa kwa {{units:mshahara wa chini ya saa moja|asarioni moja}} tu.

vi.L: Chẳng phải hai con chim sẻ bán được một đồng át-xa-ri-ôn sao?
vi.B: Hai con chim sẻ chỉ bán được {{units:một đồng xu nhỏ|một đồng át-xa-ri-ôn}}, phải không?
vi.R: Hai con chim sẻ chỉ bán được {{units:một đồng xu nhỏ|một đồng át-xa-ri-ôn}}.

ko.L: 참새 두 마리가 한 앗사리온에 팔리지 않느냐?
ko.B: 참새 두 마리가 {{units:한 푼|한 앗사리온}}에 팔리지 않느냐?
ko.R: 참새 두 마리는 {{units:동전 한 닢|한 앗사리온}}에 팔린다.

pt.L: Não se vendem dois pardais por um asse?
pt.B: Dois pardais são vendidos por {{units:um centavo|um asse}}, não são?
pt.R: Dois pardais são vendidos por só {{units:um centavo|um asse}}.

decisions.choice: two sparrows for an assarion: almost worthless birds
decisions.reason: An assarion was a small Roman copper coin worth a sixteenth of a denarius, a laborer's daily wage. Sparrows were the cheapest birds sold for food.

decisions.choice: {{units:a penny|an assarion}}
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use a small modern coin by default, with the original coin as the alternative. Literal keeps the original coin.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
alternatives: Are not two sparrows sold for a penny?
decisions.reason: The question expects "yes"; Readable gives the answer.

decisions.choice: un as (L); {{units:un centime|un as}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: The coin is the Roman as, its usual French name, as in Luke 12:6. Balanced and Readable give a small modern coin by default, as the English does with "a penny"; French readers know the centime.

decisions.choice: asarioni moja (L); {{units:mshahara wa chini ya saa moja|asarioni moja}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: The coin was a small Roman copper, a sixteenth of a day's wage (meaning decision m1). As with other coins (John 6:7, 12:5), the modern reading gives it as wages, where the English gives "a penny".

decisions.choice: un as (L); {{units:menos de una hora de salario|un as}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: The coin was a small Roman copper, a sixteenth of a day's wage (meaning decision m1). As with other coins (John 6:7, 12:5), the modern reading gives it as wages, where the English gives "a penny". "As" is the Spanish name of the Roman coin.

decisions.choice: "một đồng át-xa-ri-ôn" (L); {{units:một đồng xu nhỏ|một đồng át-xa-ri-ôn}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese has no coin like the English "penny"; "một đồng xu nhỏ" says what matters, that the birds were almost worthless (meaning decision). The alternative gives the Roman coin in Vietnamese syllables, which Literal keeps.

decisions.choice: {{units:한 푼|한 앗사리온}} (B), {{units:동전 한 닢|한 앗사리온}} (R); Literal keeps "앗사리온"
decisions.reason: As the Korean Matthew 5:26: the modern default is a word for a coin of almost no value, which is the point (meaning decision); the original coin is the alternative. Literal keeps the original unit. The particle "에" fits both forms.

decisions.choice: um asse (L); {{units:um centavo|um asse}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Asse" is the Portuguese name of the Roman coin. Balanced and Readable default to the smallest Brazilian coin, "um centavo", as the English uses "a penny", with the original coin as the alternative (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 7).

source.text: καὶ ἓν ἐξ αὐτῶν οὐ πεσεῖται ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἄνευ τοῦ πατρὸς ὑμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And one of them not will fall to the ground apart from the Father of you.

en.L: And not one of them will fall to the ground apart from your Father.
en.B: Yet not one of them falls to the ground apart from your Father.
en.R: But not even one of them falls to the ground and dies unless your Father allows it.

es.L: Y ni uno de ellos caerá a tierra sin {{plural_you:el Padre de ustedes|vuestro Padre}}.
es.B: Y, aun así, ninguno de ellos cae al suelo al margen de {{plural_you:el Padre de ustedes|vuestro Padre}}.
es.R: Pero ni uno solo de ellos cae al suelo y muere si {{plural_you:el Padre de ustedes|vuestro Padre}} no lo permite.

fr.L: Et pas un d’entre eux ne tombera à terre sans votre Père.
fr.B: Pourtant, pas un seul ne tombe à terre en dehors de votre Père.
fr.R: Mais pas un seul ne tombe par terre et ne meurt sans que votre Père le permette.

sw.L: Na hata mmoja wao hataanguka juu ya nchi pasipo Baba yenu.
sw.B: Lakini hakuna hata mmoja wao anayeanguka chini pasipo Baba yenu.
sw.R: Lakini hata mmoja wao haanguki chini na kufa Baba yenu asipokubali.

vi.L: Thế mà không một con nào trong chúng rơi xuống đất ngoài [ý] Cha các con.
vi.B: Thế nhưng không một con nào rơi xuống đất mà Cha các con không cho phép.
vi.R: Nhưng không một con nào rơi xuống đất mà chết nếu Cha các con không cho phép.

ko.L: 그러나 그것들 가운데 하나도 너희 아버지의 [뜻] 없이는 땅에 떨어지지 않을 것이다.
ko.B: 그러나 너희 아버지께서 허락하지 않으시면, 그 가운데 한 마리도 땅에 떨어지지 않는다.
ko.R: 그러나 너희 아버지께서 허락하지 않으시면, 그 가운데 한 마리도 땅에 떨어져 죽지 않는다.

pt.L: E nem um deles cairá na terra sem o Pai de vocês.
pt.B: Mesmo assim, nenhum deles cai no chão sem o Pai de vocês.
pt.R: Mas nem um só deles cai no chão e morre sem que o Pai de vocês permita.

decisions.choice: apart from your Father: without his will and care
decisions.reason: The phrase is short. It means nothing happens to even a sparrow outside the Father's rule. Some manuscripts add "will" to make this plain.

decisions.choice: fall to the ground: die
decisions.reason: A bird falling to the ground is one that dies.

decisions.choice: and dies unless your Father allows it
decisions.reason: Readable spells out both phrases, following the meaning decisions.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:el Padre de ustedes|vuestro Padre}}
decisions.reason: "Su Padre" could be read as the sparrows' father, so the Latin American form says "el Padre de ustedes".

decisions.choice: "ngoài [ý] Cha các con" (L)
decisions.reason: "apart from your Father" means without his will and care (meaning decision); Vietnamese needs the bracketed noun to say it.

decisions.choice: "아버지의 [뜻] 없이는" (L); "아버지께서 허락하지 않으시면" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Apart from your Father" means without his will and care (meaning decision); Korean "아버지 없이는" alone would say the Father is absent, so Literal brackets "뜻" and Balanced and Readable say it with the verb, as the English Readable does.

source.text: ὑμῶν δὲ καὶ αἱ τρίχες τῆς κεφαλῆς πᾶσαι ἠριθμημέναι εἰσίν.

records.literal_gloss: Of you and even the hairs of the head all numbered are.

en.L: But even the hairs of your head are all numbered.
en.B: As for you, even the hairs on your head have all been counted.
en.R: God even knows how many hairs are on your head.

es.L: Y en cuanto a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, hasta los cabellos de la cabeza están todos contados.
es.B: En cuanto a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, hasta los cabellos de la cabeza han sido contados uno por uno.
es.R: Dios sabe incluso cuántos cabellos {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} en la cabeza.

fr.L: Mais même les cheveux de votre tête sont tous comptés.
fr.B: Quant à vous, même vos cheveux ont tous été comptés, un par un.
fr.R: Dieu sait même combien de cheveux vous avez sur la tête.

sw.L: Lakini kwa habari yenu, hata nywele za kichwa zote zimehesabiwa.
sw.B: Kwa upande wenu, hata kila unywele wa kichwa chenu umehesabiwa.
sw.R: Mungu anajua hata idadi ya nywele zilizo vichwani mwenu.

vi.L: Còn các con, ngay cả tóc trên đầu cũng đã được đếm hết rồi.
vi.B: Còn các con, ngay cả từng sợi tóc trên đầu các con cũng đã được đếm cả rồi.
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời còn biết trên đầu các con có bao nhiêu sợi tóc.

ko.L: 너희에게는 머리카락까지도 모두 세어져 있다.
ko.B: 하나님께서는 너희 머리카락까지도 하나하나 다 세어 두셨다.
ko.R: 하나님께서는 너희 머리카락이 몇 개인지까지 다 알고 계신다.

pt.L: E até os cabelos da cabeça de vocês estão todos contados.
pt.B: Quanto a vocês, até os cabelos da cabeça já foram todos contados.
pt.R: Deus sabe até quantos fios de cabelo vocês têm na cabeça.

decisions.choice: your hairs are numbered: God has counted them
decisions.reason: "Your" stands first for emphasis: if God cares for sparrows, how much more for you. The passive points to God.

decisions.choice: God even knows
decisions.reason: Readable names God and says what the counting shows.

decisions.choice: "하나님께서는 ... 세어 두셨다" (B)
decisions.reason: God has counted them (meaning decision); a Korean passive of counting sounds stiff, so Balanced names the one who counts, as Readable does.

source.text: μὴ οὖν φοβεῖσθε· πολλῶν στρουθίων διαφέρετε ὑμεῖς.

records.literal_gloss: Not therefore fear; than many sparrows are worth more you.

en.L: So do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows.
en.B: So do not be afraid. You are worth more than a whole flock of sparrows.
en.R: So do not be afraid. You are worth much more to God than many sparrows.

es.L: Por tanto, no {{plural_you:teman|temáis}}; más que muchos gorriones {{plural_you:valen ustedes|valéis vosotros}}.
es.B: Así que no {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo: {{plural_you:ustedes valen|vosotros valéis}} más que una bandada entera de gorriones.
es.R: Así que no {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo. Para Dios, {{plural_you:ustedes valen|vosotros valéis}} mucho más que muchos gorriones.

fr.L: Ne craignez donc pas ; vous valez plus que beaucoup de moineaux.
fr.B: N’ayez donc pas peur. Vous valez plus que toute une volée de moineaux.
fr.R: Alors n’ayez pas peur. Pour Dieu, vous valez bien plus que beaucoup de moineaux.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo msiogope; kuliko shomoro wengi, ninyi mna thamani zaidi.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo msiogope. Ninyi mna thamani zaidi kuliko kundi zima la shomoro.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo msiogope. Mbele za Mungu mna thamani kubwa zaidi kuliko shomoro wengi.

vi.L: Vậy đừng sợ; các con quý hơn nhiều chim sẻ.
vi.B: Vậy, đừng sợ. Các con quý hơn cả một đàn chim sẻ.
vi.R: Vậy, đừng sợ. Đối với Đức Chúa Trời, các con quý hơn nhiều con chim sẻ.

ko.L: 그러므로 두려워하지 마라. 너희는 많은 참새보다 더 귀하다.
ko.B: 그러므로 두려워하지 마라. 너희는 참새 떼보다 훨씬 더 귀하다.
ko.R: 그러니 무서워하지 마라. 하나님께는 너희가 참새 여러 마리보다 훨씬 더 귀하다.

pt.L: Portanto, não temam; vocês valem mais do que muitos pardais.
pt.B: Portanto, não tenham medo. Vocês valem mais do que um bando inteiro de pardais.
pt.R: Por isso, não tenham medo. Para Deus, vocês valem muito mais do que muitos pardais.

decisions.choice: worth more than many sparrows: from the lesser to the greater
decisions.reason: If God cares for birds sold for almost nothing, he cares far more for his children (6:26).

decisions.choice: to God
decisions.reason: Readable says whose valuing is meant.

source.text: Πᾶς οὖν ὅστις ὁμολογήσει ἐν ἐμοὶ ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ὁμολογήσω κἀγὼ ἐν αὐτῷ ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς·

records.literal_gloss: Everyone therefore who will confess in me before the men, will confess also I in him before the Father of me the in heavens;

en.L: Everyone therefore who will acknowledge {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} before {{gender:people|men}}, I also will acknowledge {{gender:them|him}} before {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father who [is] in [the] heavens;
en.B: So everyone who openly confesses {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} before others, I also will confess before {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father in heaven.
en.R: Some people will say openly that they are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} followers. I will tell {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father in heaven that they belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: Todo aquel, pues, que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} reconozca delante de {{gender:la gente|los hombres}}, también yo lo reconoceré delante de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Padre que [está] en [los] cielos;
es.B: Así que a todo el que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} reconozca abiertamente delante de los demás, yo también lo reconoceré delante de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Padre que está en el cielo.
es.R: Algunas personas dirán abiertamente que son {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} seguidores. Yo le diré a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Padre que está en el cielo que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} pertenecen.

fr.L: Quiconque donc {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} reconnaîtra devant les {{gender:gens|hommes}}, {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} aussi je le reconnaîtrai devant {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père qui [est] dans les cieux ;
fr.B: Ainsi, quiconque {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} reconnaîtra ouvertement devant les autres, je le reconnaîtrai, {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} aussi, devant {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père qui est au ciel.
fr.R: Certaines personnes diront ouvertement qu’elles sont {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} disciples. Alors je dirai à {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père qui est au ciel qu’elles sont à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.

sw.L: Basi kila mtu atakayenitambua mbele ya watu, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitamtambua mbele ya Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} aliye mbinguni;
sw.B: Basi kila mtu atakayesema waziwazi mbele ya watu kwamba yeye ni {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitamtambua mbele ya Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} aliye mbinguni.
sw.R: Watu wengine watasema waziwazi kwamba wao ni wafuasi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}. Nami nitamwambia Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} aliye mbinguni kwamba wao ni {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}.

vi.L: Vậy, mọi người xưng nhận {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} trước mặt người ta, thì chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng sẽ xưng nhận người ấy trước mặt Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, Đấng ở trên các tầng trời;
vi.B: Vậy, ai công khai xưng nhận {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} trước mặt người ta, thì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng sẽ xưng nhận người ấy trước mặt Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ở trên trời.
vi.R: Ai dám nói công khai trước mặt người khác rằng mình thuộc về {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, thì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng sẽ nói với Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ở trên trời rằng người ấy thuộc về {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.

ko.L: 그러므로 누구든지 사람들 앞에서 나를 시인하는 사람은, 나도 하늘에 계신 내 아버지 앞에서 그를 시인할 것이다.
ko.B: 그러므로 누구든지 사람들 앞에서 나를 떳떳이 시인하면, 나도 하늘에 계신 내 아버지 앞에서 그 사람을 시인할 것이다.
ko.R: 누구든지 사람들 앞에서 자기가 내 제자라고 떳떳이 말하면, 나도 하늘에 계신 내 아버지께 그 사람이 내 사람이라고 말할 것이다.

pt.L: Portanto, todo aquele que se declarar por {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} diante {{gender:das pessoas|dos homens}}, também eu me declararei por ele diante do {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} Pai que [está] nos céus;
pt.B: Assim, quem se declarar abertamente por {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} diante dos outros, por esse eu também me declararei diante do {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} Pai, que está no céu.
pt.R: Algumas pessoas vão dizer abertamente que me seguem. Eu vou dizer ao {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} Pai, que está no céu, que elas pertencem a {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}.

decisions.choice: confess in me: openly declare that one belongs to me
decisions.reason: The phrase follows an Aramaic way of speaking. It means to stand openly on someone's side.

decisions.choice: before my Father: at the judgment
decisions.reason: Jesus pictures himself speaking for his followers when God judges (7:21-23; 25:31-34).

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}; {{gender:them|him}}
decisions.reason: The words apply to everyone, so the inclusive forms are the default.

decisions.choice: les {{gender:gens|hommes}}; "le" with no gender span (L)
decisions.reason: The setting goes on the noun French must choose, as in Luke 12:8. The pronoun "le" refers back to "quiconque" and is ordinary generic French, so it takes none, unlike the English {{gender:them|him}}. The same in 10:33.

decisions.choice: kutambua (to own, acknowledge as one's own)
decisions.reason: To declare openly that one belongs to Jesus, and for him to own that person (meaning decision m1). "Kutambua" is to recognise and own someone; "kukiri" is more often to admit a fact. "Watu" already includes men and women, so there is no gender span.

decisions.choice: {{gender:la gente|los hombres}}; lo, with no span
decisions.reason: "Los hombres" means people in general, so Literal has the same gender span as the English. Spanish "lo" for "everyone who" is the ordinary generic form and has no inclusive alternative, so it takes none.

decisions.choice: "xưng nhận" (L, B); "nói ... rằng mình thuộc về Ta" (R)
decisions.reason: To confess "in me" is to declare openly that one belongs to Jesus (meaning decision). "người ta" and "người ấy" include men and women, so the English Literal gender spans have no counterpart; the same in 10:33.

decisions.choice: "Đấng ở trên các tầng trời" (L); "ở trên trời" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The forms settled for "my Father in the heavens" in Matthew; also in 10:33.

decisions.choice: "시인하다" (L, B); "하늘에 계신 내 아버지" at every level; no gender span for "사람들"
decisions.reason: To confess "in me" is to declare openly that one belongs to Jesus (meaning decision); "시인하다" is to acknowledge openly, while "고백하다" now suggests confessing a fault. "하늘에 계신" for the Father in the heavens, as the Korean Matthew 7:11 and 7:21 at every level. Korean "사람" already includes men and women.

decisions.choice: se declarar por mim
decisions.reason: "Declarar-se por alguém" is to take someone's side openly, which is what the idiom means (m1), and like the Greek it takes a preposition. "Confessar" in Portuguese suggests admitting a sin.

decisions.choice: por ele, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The English needs a setting on "them|him". In Portuguese "ele" here refers back to "todo aquele que", which already means anyone, and is ordinary generic Portuguese (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 7); only "homens" takes the setting.

source.text: ὅστις δ’ ἂν ἀρνήσηταί με ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ἀρνήσομαι κἀγὼ αὐτὸν ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: whoever but denies me before the men, will deny also I him before the Father of me the in heavens.

en.L: but whoever denies {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} before {{gender:people|men}}, I also will deny {{gender:them|him}} before {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father who [is] in [the] heavens.
en.B: But whoever denies {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in front of people will be denied by {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in the presence of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father in heaven.
en.R: But some people will say in front of others that they do not know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I will tell {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father in heaven that I do not know them.

es.L: pero quien reniegue de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} delante de {{gender:la gente|los hombres}}, también yo renegaré de él delante de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Padre que [está] en [los] cielos.
es.B: Pero quien reniegue de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} ante los demás será rechazado por {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} en presencia de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Padre que está en el cielo.
es.R: Pero algunas personas dirán delante de otros que no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} conocen. Yo le diré a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Padre que está en el cielo que no las conozco.

fr.L: mais quiconque {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} reniera devant les {{gender:gens|hommes}}, {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} aussi je le renierai devant {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père qui [est] dans les cieux.
fr.B: Mais celui qui {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} renie devant les autres sera renié par {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} en présence de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père qui est au ciel.
fr.R: Mais d’autres diront devant tout le monde qu’ils ne {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} connaissent pas. Alors je dirai à {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père qui est au ciel que je ne les connais pas.

sw.L: lakini yeyote atakayenikataa mbele ya watu, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitamkataa mbele ya Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} aliye mbinguni.
sw.B: Lakini yeyote atakayenikataa mbele ya watu atakataliwa na {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} mbele ya Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} aliye mbinguni.
sw.R: Lakini watu wengine watasema mbele ya wengine kwamba hawanijui. Nami nitamwambia Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} aliye mbinguni kwamba siwajui.

vi.L: nhưng ai chối {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} trước mặt người ta, thì chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng sẽ chối người ấy trước mặt Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, Đấng ở trên các tầng trời.
vi.B: Nhưng ai chối bỏ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} trước mặt người ta, thì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng sẽ chối bỏ người ấy trước mặt Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ở trên trời.
vi.R: Nhưng ai nói trước mặt người khác rằng mình không biết {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, thì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng sẽ nói với Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ở trên trời rằng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không biết người ấy.

ko.L: 그러나 누구든지 사람들 앞에서 나를 부인하는 사람은, 나도 하늘에 계신 내 아버지 앞에서 그를 부인할 것이다.
ko.B: 그러나 누구든지 사람들 앞에서 나를 부인하면, 나도 하늘에 계신 내 아버지 앞에서 그 사람을 부인할 것이다.
ko.R: 그러나 누구든지 사람들 앞에서 나를 모른다고 말하면, 나도 하늘에 계신 내 아버지께 그 사람을 모른다고 말할 것이다.

pt.L: mas quem me negar diante {{gender:das pessoas|dos homens}}, também eu o negarei diante do {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} Pai que [está] nos céus.
pt.B: Mas quem me negar diante das pessoas será negado por {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} na presença do {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} Pai, que está no céu.
pt.R: Mas algumas pessoas vão dizer diante dos outros que não me conhecem. Eu vou dizer ao {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} Pai, que está no céu, que não as conheço.

decisions.choice: deny me: refuse to own me, disown me
decisions.reason: Peter does this in 26:70-74. To deny Jesus is to say one has nothing to do with him.

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}; {{gender:them|him}}
decisions.reason: As in 10:32.

decisions.choice: will be denied by me
decisions.reason: Balanced turns the second clause into the passive to keep the sentence plain.

decisions.choice: kukataa (to disown)
decisions.reason: To refuse to own someone (meaning decision m1). "Kukataa" is to reject or disown; "kukana" is mostly to deny that something is so.

decisions.choice: renegar de
decisions.reason: To refuse to own someone, to disown him (meaning decision m1). "Renegar de" says that plainly; "negar" more often means to say something is not true.

decisions.choice: "chối" (L); "chối bỏ" (B)
decisions.reason: To deny is to refuse to own, to disown (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "부인하다" (L, B); "모른다고 말하다" (R)
decisions.reason: To deny is to disown (meaning decision); "부인하다" is the word of Peter's denial in the Korean John 13:38 and 18:25-27, which this saying anticipates. Readable says the plain thing.

decisions.choice: me negar, me conhecem, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: As in 5:11: an unstressed "me" before the verb is an ordinary clitic, and capitalising it reads oddly in Portuguese; the stressed "mim" and the possessives carry the setting, as the English "me" and "my" do.

source.text: Μὴ νομίσητε ὅτι ἦλθον βαλεῖν εἰρήνην ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν· οὐκ ἦλθον βαλεῖν εἰρήνην ἀλλὰ μάχαιραν.

records.literal_gloss: Not think that I came to bring peace on the earth; not I came to bring peace but a sword.

en.L: Do not think that I came to bring peace on the earth; I did not come to bring peace, but a sword.
en.B: Do not imagine that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} coming was to bring peace on earth. I came to bring a sword, not peace.
en.R: Do not think I came to bring peace to everyone on earth. I did not come to bring peace. I came to bring a sword that divides people.

es.L: No {{plural_you:piensen|penséis}} que vine a poner paz sobre la tierra; no vine a poner paz, sino espada.
es.B: No {{plural_you:imaginen|imaginéis}} que {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} venida tenía como fin traer paz a la tierra. Vine a traer espada, no paz.
es.R: No {{plural_you:piensen|penséis}} que vine a traer paz a todos en la tierra. No vine a traer paz. Vine a traer una espada que divide a la gente.

fr.L: Ne pensez pas que je suis venu apporter la paix sur la terre ; je ne suis pas venu apporter la paix, mais l’épée.
fr.B: N’allez pas imaginer que je suis venu apporter la paix sur la terre. Je suis venu apporter l’épée, non la paix.
fr.R: Ne pensez pas que je suis venu apporter la paix à tous sur la terre. Je ne suis pas venu apporter la paix. Je suis venu apporter une épée qui sépare les gens.

sw.L: Msifikiri kwamba nilikuja kuweka amani juu ya dunia; sikuja kuweka amani, ila upanga.
sw.B: Msidhani kwamba kuja {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}} kulikuwa kwa ajili ya kuleta amani duniani. Nilikuja kuleta upanga, si amani.
sw.R: Msifikiri kwamba nilikuja kuleta amani kwa kila mtu duniani. Sikuja kuleta amani. Nilikuja kuleta upanga unaowatenganisha watu.

vi.L: Đừng tưởng rằng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đến để đem bình an trên đất; {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không đến để đem bình an, nhưng [để đem] gươm giáo.
vi.B: Đừng nghĩ rằng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đến để đem bình an cho thế gian. {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đến không phải để đem bình an, mà để đem gươm giáo.
vi.R: Đừng nghĩ rằng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đến để đem bình an cho mọi người trên đất. Ta không đến để đem bình an. Ta đến để đem gươm giáo, là sự chia rẽ giữa người ta với nhau.

ko.L: 내가 땅에 평화를 주려고 왔다고 생각하지 마라. 평화를 주려고 온 것이 아니라 칼을 [주려고 왔다].
ko.B: 내가 세상에 평화를 가져오려고 왔다고 생각하지 마라. 나는 평화가 아니라 칼을 가져오려고 왔다.
ko.R: 내가 세상 모든 사람에게 평화를 주려고 왔다고 생각하지 마라. 나는 평화를 주려고 오지 않았다. 사람들을 서로 갈라놓는 칼을 주려고 왔다.

pt.L: Não pensem que vim trazer paz sobre a terra; não vim trazer paz, mas espada.
pt.B: Não imaginem que a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} vinda foi para trazer paz à terra. Eu vim trazer espada, e não paz.
pt.R: Não pensem que eu vim trazer paz para todos na terra. Eu não vim trazer paz. Eu vim trazer uma espada que divide as pessoas.

decisions.choice: a sword: division, not war
decisions.reason: Verses 35-36 explain the sword: it cuts families apart. Luke 12:51 has "division". Jesus's followers are not to fight with swords (26:52).

decisions.choice: not peace: the result of his coming, not its aim
alternatives: Jesus does not care about peace
decisions.reason: Jesus blesses peacemakers (5:9). But because people respond to him in different ways, his coming divides even families.

decisions.choice: bring: literally "throw" or "cast"
decisions.reason: The verb suggests something cast onto the earth with force.

decisions.choice: a sword that divides people
decisions.reason: Readable says what the sword stands for.

decisions.choice: poner
decisions.reason: The verb is literally "throw" or "cast" (meaning decision m3). "Echar paz" is not Spanish; "poner" keeps the picture of placing something on the earth.

decisions.choice: "gươm giáo"; "sự chia rẽ" added (R)
decisions.reason: The sword is division, not war (meaning decision); Readable says so, as the English Readable does. "trên đất" (L) keeps "on the earth"; Balanced says "thế gian", the people of the world.

decisions.choice: "평화" (not "평안"); "칼"; "사람들을 서로 갈라놓는 칼" (R)
decisions.reason: The peace here is peace among people on earth, set against division (meaning decision), so the everyday "평화", not the greeting's "평안" of 10:13; "평안" stays the key term for the peace Jesus gives in John. The sword stands for division, not war (meaning decision), which Readable says, as the English Readable does.

source.text: ἦλθον γὰρ διχάσαι ἄνθρωπον κατὰ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ καὶ θυγατέρα κατὰ τῆς μητρὸς αὐτῆς καὶ νύμφην κατὰ τῆς πενθερᾶς αὐτῆς, καὶ ἐχθροὶ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου οἱ οἰκιακοὶ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: I came for to set at variance a man against the father of him and a daughter against the mother of her and a daughter-in-law against the mother-in-law of her, \v 36 and enemies of the man the household of him.

en.L: For I came to set a man against his father, and a daughter against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; \v 36 and the enemies of the {{gender:person|man}} [will be] the members of {{gender:their|his}} household.
en.B: My coming will set son against father, daughter against mother, and daughter-in-law against mother-in-law. \v 36 People's enemies will be those of their own household.
en.R: I came to turn sons against their fathers and daughters against their mothers. I came to turn daughters-in-law against their mothers-in-law. \v 36 A person's enemies will be people in their own family.

es.L: Porque vine a enfrentar a un hombre contra su padre, y a una hija contra su madre, y a una nuera contra su suegra; \v 36 y los enemigos {{gender:de la persona|del hombre}} [serán] los de su casa.
es.B: Mi venida enfrentará al hijo con su padre, a la hija con su madre y a la nuera con su suegra. \v 36 Los enemigos de cada uno serán los de su propia familia.
es.R: Vine a poner a los hijos en contra de sus padres y a las hijas en contra de sus madres. Vine a poner a las nueras en contra de sus suegras. \v 36 Los enemigos de una persona serán los de su propia familia.

fr.L: Car je suis venu dresser un homme contre son père, une fille contre sa mère, et une belle-fille contre sa belle-mère ; \v 36 et les ennemis de {{gender:chacun|l’homme}} [seront] les gens de sa maison.
fr.B: Je suis venu dresser le fils contre son père, la fille contre sa mère, la belle-fille contre sa belle-mère. \v 36 On aura pour ennemis les gens de sa propre maison.
fr.R: Je suis venu pour que les fils soient contre leur père, et les filles contre leur mère. Je suis venu pour que les belles-filles soient contre leur belle-mère. \v 36 Les ennemis de chacun seront les gens de sa propre famille.

sw.L: Kwa maana nilikuja kumfarakanisha mtu na baba yake, na binti na mama yake, na mkaza mwana na mama mkwe wake; \v 36 na adui wa mtu [watakuwa] watu wa nyumba yake.
sw.B: Kuja {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}} kutamfarakanisha mwana na baba yake, binti na mama yake, na mkaza mwana na mama mkwe wake. \v 36 Adui wa mtu watakuwa watu wa nyumba yake mwenyewe.
sw.R: Nilikuja kuwageuza wana dhidi ya baba zao, na binti dhidi ya mama zao. Nilikuja kuwageuza wakaza wana dhidi ya mama wakwe zao. \v 36 Adui wa mtu watakuwa watu wa familia yake mwenyewe.

vi.L: Vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đến để làm cho con trai nghịch với cha mình, con gái nghịch với mẹ mình, con dâu nghịch với mẹ chồng mình; \v 36 và kẻ thù của người ta [sẽ là] chính những người nhà mình.
vi.B: Vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đến để khiến con trai chống lại cha, con gái chống lại mẹ, con dâu chống lại mẹ chồng. \v 36 Kẻ thù của mỗi người lại là chính những người trong nhà mình.
vi.R: Ta đến để làm cho con trai chống lại cha mình, con gái chống lại mẹ mình. Ta đến để làm cho con dâu chống lại mẹ chồng mình. \v 36 Kẻ thù của một người sẽ là những người trong chính gia đình người ấy.

ko.L: 내가 온 것은 사람이 자기 아버지와, 딸이 자기 어머니와, 며느리가 자기 시어머니와 맞서게 하려는 것이기 때문이다. \v 36 그리고 사람의 원수가 자기 집안 식구들일 것이다.
ko.B: 나는 아들이 아버지와, 딸이 어머니와, 며느리가 시어머니와 맞서게 하려고 왔다. \v 36 사람의 원수가 바로 자기 집안 식구일 것이다.
ko.R: 나는 아들이 아버지에게, 딸이 어머니에게 등을 돌리게 하려고 왔다. 며느리가 시어머니에게 등을 돌리게 하려고 왔다. \v 36 사람의 원수가 바로 자기 가족이 될 것이다.

pt.L: Pois eu vim colocar o homem contra o seu pai, e a filha contra a sua mãe, e a nora contra a sua sogra; \v 36 e os inimigos {{gender:da pessoa|do homem}} [serão] os da sua casa.
pt.B: A {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} vinda vai pôr o filho contra o pai, a filha contra a mãe e a nora contra a sogra. \v 36 Os inimigos de cada um serão os da sua própria casa.
pt.R: Eu vim colocar os filhos contra os pais e as filhas contra as mães. Eu vim colocar as noras contra as sogras. \v 36 Os inimigos de uma pessoa vão ser as pessoas da própria família dela.

decisions.choice: Micah 7:6
decisions.reason: Jesus takes up Micah's words about a time when families turn on each other. In Micah the son dishonors his father; here the division comes because some follow Jesus and others do not.

decisions.choice: a man against his father: a son
decisions.reason: The pairs are family members, and Micah 7:6 has "son".

decisions.choice: the man's enemies: anyone's
alternatives: the man of the first line only
decisions.reason: The last line is a general saying, as in Micah, and applies to women and men alike.

decisions.choice: son
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say which family member is meant. Specific relatives take no gender span.

decisions.choice: {{gender:person|man}}; {{gender:their|his}}
decisions.reason: The last line is general, so the inclusive form is the default.

decisions.choice: les ennemis de {{gender:chacun|l’homme}}; "sa maison" with no span (L)
decisions.reason: The last line is general (m3). French "chacun" says "anyone" plainly, with the traditional "l’homme" as the alternative; the possessive "sa" needs no setting, unlike the English {{gender:their|his}}.

decisions.choice: mkaza mwana; mama mkwe
decisions.reason: "Mkaza mwana" is a son's wife; "mkwe" alone can be any in-law, so it would not say which woman is set against which.

decisions.choice: "con trai" for "a man" against his father; "người ta", "mỗi người" with no gender span
decisions.reason: "a man against his father" means a son (meaning decision), and the enemies are anyone's (meaning decision); Vietnamese words for people are inclusive, so the English Literal gender spans have no counterpart. The words of Micah 7:6.

decisions.choice: "사람" (L), "아들" (B, R) for the man set against his father; "사람의 원수" with no gender span
decisions.reason: The man set against his father is a son (meaning decision); Literal keeps the Greek word, Balanced and Readable say "son", as the English does. In 10:36 anyone's enemies are meant (meaning decision), and Korean "사람" already says so.

source.text: ὁ φιλῶν πατέρα ἢ μητέρα ὑπὲρ ἐμὲ οὐκ ἔστιν μου ἄξιος· καὶ ὁ φιλῶν υἱὸν ἢ θυγατέρα ὑπὲρ ἐμὲ οὐκ ἔστιν μου ἄξιος·

records.literal_gloss: The loving father or mother above me not is of me worthy; and the loving son or daughter above me not is of me worthy;

en.L: The one who loves father or mother more than {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is not worthy of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; and the one who loves son or daughter more than {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is not worthy of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}};
en.B: Whoever puts love for father or mother above {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is not worthy of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and whoever puts love for son or daughter above {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is not worthy of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: People who love their father or mother more than they love {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} do not deserve to be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} followers. People who love their son or daughter more than they love {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} do not deserve to be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} followers.

es.L: Quien quiere a padre o madre por encima de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} no es digno de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}; y quien quiere a hijo o hija por encima de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} no es digno de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}};
es.B: Quien pone el amor a su padre o a su madre por encima de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} no es digno de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, y quien pone el amor a su hijo o a su hija por encima de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} no es digno de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.R: Los que aman a su padre o a su madre más que a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} no merecen ser {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} seguidores. Los que aman a su hijo o a su hija más que a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} no merecen ser {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} seguidores.

fr.L: Celui qui aime père ou mère plus que {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} n’est pas digne de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ; et celui qui aime fils ou fille plus que {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} n’est pas digne de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ;
fr.B: Celui qui fait passer son amour pour son père ou sa mère avant {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} n’est pas digne de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, et celui qui fait passer son amour pour son fils ou sa fille avant {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} n’est pas digne de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.R: Ceux qui aiment leur père ou leur mère plus qu’ils ne {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}aiment ne méritent pas d’être {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} disciples. Ceux qui aiment leur fils ou leur fille plus qu’ils ne {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}aiment ne méritent pas d’être {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} disciples.

sw.L: Anayempenda baba au mama juu ya {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} hanistahili; na anayempenda mwana au binti juu ya {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} hanistahili;
sw.B: Yeyote anayempenda baba au mama kuliko anavyonipenda {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} hanistahili; na yeyote anayempenda mwana au binti kuliko anavyonipenda {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} hanistahili.
sw.R: Watu wanaompenda baba yao au mama yao kuliko wanavyonipenda {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} hawastahili kuwa wafuasi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}. Watu wanaompenda mwana wao au binti yao kuliko wanavyonipenda {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} hawastahili kuwa wafuasi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}.

vi.L: Ai yêu cha hay mẹ hơn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thì không xứng đáng với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; và ai yêu con trai hay con gái hơn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thì không xứng đáng với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}};
vi.B: Ai yêu cha mẹ hơn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thì không xứng đáng với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Ai yêu con trai hay con gái hơn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thì không xứng đáng với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.R: Ai yêu cha mẹ mình hơn yêu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thì không xứng đáng làm môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Ai yêu con trai hay con gái mình hơn yêu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thì không xứng đáng làm môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.

ko.L: 나보다 아버지나 어머니를 더 사랑하는 사람은 나에게 합당하지 않다. 그리고 나보다 아들이나 딸을 더 사랑하는 사람도 나에게 합당하지 않다.
ko.B: 나보다 아버지나 어머니를 더 사랑하는 사람은 나에게 합당하지 않다. 나보다 아들이나 딸을 더 사랑하는 사람도 나에게 합당하지 않다.
ko.R: 자기 아버지나 어머니를 나보다 더 사랑하는 사람은 내 제자가 될 자격이 없다. 자기 아들이나 딸을 나보다 더 사랑하는 사람도 내 제자가 될 자격이 없다.

pt.L: Aquele que ama pai ou mãe acima de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} não é digno de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}; e aquele que ama filho ou filha acima de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} não é digno de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}};
pt.B: Quem coloca o amor pelo pai ou pela mãe acima de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} não é digno de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, e quem coloca o amor pelo filho ou pela filha acima de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} não é digno de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}.
pt.R: Quem ama o pai ou a mãe mais do que a {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} não merece ser {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} seguidor. Quem ama o filho ou a filha mais do que a {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} não merece ser {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} seguidor.

decisions.choice: worthy of me: fit to belong to me as my disciple
decisions.reason: The word is used of what fits or deserves something. Jesus says who truly belongs to him; he is not grading people's merit.

decisions.choice: love more than me: put before me
decisions.reason: Jesus asks for first place, not for lack of love at home. Luke 14:26 says the same with the stronger idiom "hate". Jesus also upholds honor for parents (15:4).

decisions.choice: do not deserve to be my followers
decisions.reason: Readable says what being worthy of Jesus means.

decisions.choice: "không xứng đáng làm môn đồ của Ta" (R)
decisions.reason: Worthy of me means fit to belong to me as my disciple (meaning decision). Readable says "môn đồ", the word for disciples at every level, where the English Readable says "followers"; the same in 10:38.

decisions.choice: "나에게 합당하지 않다" (L, B); "내 제자가 될 자격이 없다" (R), through 10:37-38
decisions.reason: Worthy of me means fit to belong to Jesus as his disciple (meaning decision); Readable says so, as the English Readable does.

source.text: καὶ ὃς οὐ λαμβάνει τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀκολουθεῖ ὀπίσω μου, οὐκ ἔστιν μου ἄξιος.

records.literal_gloss: and who not takes the cross of him and follows after me, not is of me worthy.

en.L: and whoever does not take {{gender:their|his}} cross and follow after {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is not worthy of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: Whoever refuses to pick up their own cross and walk behind {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is not worthy of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: People who will not carry their cross and come after {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} do not deserve to be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} followers.

es.L: y quien no carga con su cruz y viene detrás de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, no es digno de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.B: Quien se niega a tomar su propia cruz y caminar detrás de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} no es digno de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.R: Los que no quieren cargar su cruz y venir detrás de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} no merecen ser {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} seguidores.

fr.L: et celui qui ne prend pas sa croix et ne vient pas à {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} suite n’est pas digne de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.B: Celui qui refuse de prendre sa propre croix et de marcher derrière {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} n’est pas digne de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.R: Ceux qui ne veulent pas porter leur croix et venir derrière {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ne méritent pas d’être {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} disciples.

sw.L: na yeyote asiyebeba msalaba wake na kufuata nyuma {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, hanistahili.
sw.B: Yeyote anayekataa kuubeba msalaba wake mwenyewe na kutembea nyuma {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} hanistahili.
sw.R: Watu wasiotaka kubeba msalaba wao na kunifuata hawastahili kuwa wafuasi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}.

vi.L: và ai không vác thập tự giá mình mà theo sau {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thì không xứng đáng với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.B: Ai không vác thập tự giá của mình mà theo {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thì không xứng đáng với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.R: Ai không chịu vác thập tự giá của mình và đi theo {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thì không xứng đáng làm môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.

ko.L: 그리고 자기 십자가를 지고 내 뒤를 따르지 않는 사람은 나에게 합당하지 않다.
ko.B: 자기 십자가를 지고 나를 따르지 않는 사람은 나에게 합당하지 않다.
ko.R: 자기 십자가를 지고 나를 따라오지 않는 사람은 내 제자가 될 자격이 없다.

pt.L: e quem não toma a sua cruz e não segue atrás de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} não é digno de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}.
pt.B: Quem se recusa a tomar a própria cruz e a andar atrás de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} não é digno de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}.
pt.R: Quem não carrega a sua cruz e não vem atrás de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} não merece ser {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} seguidor.

decisions.choice: take his cross: as a condemned man carried his cross to execution
decisions.reason: Under Rome a condemned man carried the crossbeam to the place of death (27:32). Following Jesus means being ready to suffer and die for him. This is the first mention of the cross in Matthew, before Jesus speaks plainly of his death (16:21, 24).

decisions.choice: worthy of me: fit to belong to me as my disciple
decisions.reason: The word is used of what fits or deserves something. Jesus says who truly belongs to him; he is not grading people's merit.

decisions.choice: follow after me (L); walk behind me (B)
decisions.reason: The words picture walking behind Jesus on the road to the cross.

decisions.choice: "thập tự giá"
decisions.reason: The Protestant word, as in Mark 8:34. A condemned man carried his cross to execution (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "자기 십자가를 지고", as the Korean Mark 8:34
decisions.reason: The picture is a condemned man carrying his cross to execution (meaning decision); Korean keeps it plainly at every level, worded as the Korean Mark 8:34 Balanced.

source.text: ὁ εὑρὼν τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἀπολέσει αὐτήν, καὶ ὁ ἀπολέσας τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ εὑρήσει αὐτήν.

records.literal_gloss: The having found the life of him will lose it, and the having lost the life of him on account of me will find it.

en.L: The one who has found {{gender:their|his}} life will lose it, and the one who has lost {{gender:their|his}} life for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sake will find it.
en.B: Those who secure their own life will lose it, and those who lose their life for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sake will find it.
en.R: People who try to keep their life for themselves will lose it. But people who give up their life for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} will find it.

es.L: El que encontró su vida la perderá, y el que perdió su vida a causa de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} la encontrará.
es.B: Quien asegura su propia vida la perderá, y quien pierde su vida por {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} la encontrará.
es.R: Los que tratan de guardar su vida para sí mismos la perderán. Pero los que entregan su vida por {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} la encontrarán.

fr.L: Celui qui a trouvé sa vie la perdra, et celui qui a perdu sa vie à cause de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} la trouvera.
fr.B: Celui qui met sa vie à l’abri la perdra, et celui qui perd sa vie pour {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} la trouvera.
fr.R: Ceux qui essaient de garder leur vie pour eux-mêmes la perdront. Mais ceux qui donnent leur vie pour {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} la trouveront.

sw.L: Aliyeyapata maisha yake atayapoteza, na aliyeyapoteza maisha yake kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} atayapata.
sw.B: Wanaoyalinda maisha yao watayapoteza, na wanaoyapoteza maisha yao kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} watayapata.
sw.R: Watu wanaojaribu kuyashika maisha yao kwa ajili yao wenyewe watayapoteza. Lakini watu wanaoyatoa maisha yao kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} watayapata.

vi.L: Ai tìm được mạng sống mình thì sẽ mất nó, còn ai mất mạng sống mình vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thì sẽ tìm lại được nó.
vi.B: Ai cố giữ lấy mạng sống mình thì sẽ mất nó, còn ai mất mạng sống mình vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thì sẽ tìm lại được nó.
vi.R: Ai cố giữ mạng sống cho riêng mình thì sẽ mất nó. Nhưng ai chịu mất mạng sống mình vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thì sẽ tìm lại được nó.

ko.L: 자기 목숨을 얻은 사람은 그것을 잃을 것이고, 나 때문에 자기 목숨을 잃은 사람은 그것을 얻을 것이다.
ko.B: 자기 목숨을 지키는 사람은 그것을 잃을 것이고, 나 때문에 자기 목숨을 잃는 사람은 그것을 얻을 것이다.
ko.R: 자기만을 위해 목숨을 지키려는 사람은 그 목숨을 잃을 것이다. 그러나 나를 위해 자기 목숨을 내놓는 사람은 그 목숨을 얻을 것이다.

pt.L: Quem achou a sua vida a perderá, e quem perdeu a sua vida por causa de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} a achará.
pt.B: Quem assegura a própria vida vai perdê-la, e quem perde a vida por causa de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} vai encontrá-la.
pt.R: Quem tenta guardar a vida só para si vai perdê-la. Mas quem dá a vida por {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} vai encontrá-la.

decisions.choice: life: one's life and self, here and in the age to come
decisions.reason: The same word is "soul" in 10:28. The saying plays on two senses: life in this world, and the true life God gives.

decisions.choice: has found: has secured or kept safe, as by denying Jesus
alternatives: has discovered the meaning of life
decisions.reason: In context, to "find" one's life is to save it by giving up following Jesus (10:33). Compare 16:25.

decisions.choice: secure (B); try to keep (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what finding means here; the second "find" keeps the word.

decisions.choice: maisha
decisions.reason: Here the word is one's life and self, here and in the age to come (meaning decision m1), lost and found; "maisha", as in John 12:25. In verse 28 the same Greek word is the soul set beside the body, "nafsi".

decisions.choice: "mạng sống" for psychē
decisions.reason: As in Mark 8:35: one's life and self, here and in the age to come (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "목숨" for psyche; "얻다" (L) and "지키다" (B, R) for the first "find"; "얻다" for the second
decisions.reason: "목숨" is the style guide's word for psyche: the life one has and can lose, here and in the age to come (meaning decision). "Has found" means has secured or kept safe (meaning decision); Literal keeps one verb, "얻다", for both finds, and Balanced and Readable say "keep" in the first.

source.text: Ὁ δεχόμενος ὑμᾶς ἐμὲ δέχεται, καὶ ὁ ἐμὲ δεχόμενος δέχεται τὸν ἀποστείλαντά με.

records.literal_gloss: The receiving you me receives, and the me receiving receives the having sent me.

en.L: The one who receives you receives {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and the one who receives {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} receives the [one] who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: To welcome you is to welcome {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and to welcome {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is to welcome {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: When people welcome you, they are welcoming {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. And when they welcome {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, they are welcoming God, who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: Quien {{plural_you:los|os}} acoge a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} acoge; y quien a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} acoge, acoge al que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} envió.
es.B: Quien {{plural_you:los|os}} acoge a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} acoge a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, y quien {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} acoge a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, acoge también al que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} envió.
es.R: Cuando alguien {{plural_you:los|os}} recibe a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} está recibiendo a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Y cuando {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} recibe a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, está recibiendo a Dios, que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} envió.

fr.L: Celui qui vous reçoit {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} reçoit, et celui qui {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} reçoit reçoit celui qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé.
fr.B: Vous accueillir, c’est {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}accueillir, et {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}accueillir, c’est accueillir celui qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé.
fr.R: Quand les gens vous accueillent, c’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} qu’ils accueillent. Et quand ils {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}accueillent, c’est Dieu qu’ils accueillent, Dieu qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé.
